weekday.text: The reward of deeds depends on intentions.
The most beloved deed to Allah is the most regular and constant, even if it is small.
None of you truly believes until he wishes for his brother what he likes for himself.
Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or keep quiet.
The strong one is not who overpowers others, but who controls himself when angry.
No one has eaten a better meal than what he earned by working with his own hands.
The best among you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it.
There are two blessings many people lose out on: health and free time.
The religion is easy. Don't overburden yourself; aim close to what is right and be glad.
Make things easy for people, not hard; give good news and do not drive them away.
Every act of goodness is charity.
A good word is charity, and removing something harmful from the road is charity.
The best among you are those with the best character.
Who most deserves my good company? 'Your mother,' three times, 'then your father.'
Whoever fulfills the needs of his brother, Allah will fulfill his needs.
A Muslim is one who avoids harming other Muslims with his tongue and hands.
Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise.
Convey from me, even if it is a single verse.
When Allah wants good for a person, He gives him understanding of the religion.
When a Muslim plants a tree and a bird, person or animal eats from it, it is charity for him.
A believer to another believer is like a building whose parts strengthen each other.
Allah loves gentleness in all matters.
May Allah have mercy on one who is easygoing when he buys, sells, and asks for repayment.
Mention Allah's name, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is near you.
Feed others, and greet those you know and those you do not know.
All of you are guardians, and each of you is responsible for those in his care.
Jibril kept urging me to be kind to neighbors until I thought he would make them heirs.
A good companion is like a musk seller: he gifts you, sells to you, or you enjoy his scent.
True wealth is not many possessions; true wealth is contentment of the soul.
Whoever wants his provision and life extended, let him keep good ties with his relatives.
There is a piece of flesh in the body: if it is sound, the whole body is sound. It is the heart.
O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness.
Anas served the Prophet (pbuh) for ten years, and he never once said 'uff' to him or blamed him.
At home, the Prophet (pbuh) kept busy serving his family, and went out when it was time to pray.
Strive for what benefits you, seek Allah's help, and do not lose heart.
Whoever walks a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise.
How wonderful the believer's affair: in good times he is grateful, in hard times patient. Both are good.
Charity does not decrease wealth, and whoever humbles himself for Allah, Allah raises him.
Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face.
Gentleness is not found in anything except that it beautifies it.
Cleanliness is half of faith, and 'Alhamdulillah' fills the scale.
When a person dies his deeds end, except three: ongoing charity, useful knowledge, a child who prays for him.
Allah does not look at your faces or your wealth, but at your hearts and your deeds.
Shall I tell you something that will make you love one another? Spread the greeting of salaam.
Look at those below you, not those above you; that keeps you from belittling Allah's favors.
Allah is pleased with a servant who says 'Alhamdulillah' when he eats and when he drinks.
Allah has prescribed excellence (ihsan) in all things.
Righteousness is good character.
When you cook a broth, add some water and share it with your neighbors.
Whoever guides someone to good gets a reward like the one who does it.
Whoever visits the sick is in the fruit garden of Paradise until he returns.
Your smile in the face of your brother is charity.
Be mindful of Allah wherever you are, follow a bad deed with a good one, and treat people well.
Nothing is heavier on the believer's scale on Judgment Day than good character.
The best of you is the one who is best to his family.
Allah, His angels, even the ant in its hole, send blessings on one who teaches people good.
Be merciful to those on earth, and the One above the heavens will show you mercy.
Whoever wakes up safe, healthy, and with food for the day, it is as if the world were gathered for him.
Whoever is not grateful to people is not grateful to Allah.
Saying 'Jazak Allahu khayran' to one who does you good is the fullest of praise.
Rely on Allah truly and He will provide for you like the birds: out hungry at dawn, back full.
A person follows the way of his close friend, so look carefully at whom you befriend.
O Allah, bless my people in their early mornings.
O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision, and accepted deeds.
Give the worker his wages before his sweat dries.
Stay with your mother, for Paradise is beneath her feet.
Man will have nothing except what he strives for.
Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves.
My Lord, increase me in knowledge.
Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger and the believers.
Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due.
Fulfill every commitment.
The believers are but brothers, so make peace between your brothers.
The servants of the Most Merciful walk gently on earth, and when the ignorant address them, they say peace.
My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small.
Repel evil with what is better, and an enemy may become a devoted friend.
Never say of anything, 'I will do that tomorrow,' without adding, 'If Allah wills.'
Those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways.
Allah does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear.
Those who restrain anger and pardon people: Allah loves the doers of good.
Start your hardest task after Fajr; mornings carry barakah.
Begin with Bismillah, and make the first hour of work your most focused.
Small daily habits, done consistently, outweigh big bursts of effort.
Plan your day around the five prayers; they are natural checkpoints.
Use the time between Asr and Maghrib to review what you finished today.
Make one sincere dua before you start something new.
Tidy your space before you work; a clear room helps a clear mind.
Call your parents today, even if only for two minutes.
Return what you borrowed and keep the promises you made.
Read one ayah with its meaning today and think about it for a while.
Give the task you keep postponing five minutes. Starting is the hardest part.
Learn one new thing today and teach it to someone at home.
Silence the distractions for one hour of deep, honest work.
Sleep early tonight so you can wake for Fajr with energy.
Write down three blessings before you sleep.
Smile at your family when you walk through the door.
Say Alhamdulillah after every finished task, however small.
Be the colleague people can trust with their work and their secrets.
Before you complain, count what is already going right.
Work with ihsan: do it well even when no one is checking.
Renew your wudu before a big task; it refreshes body and mind.
Forgive one small thing today and let it go.
Ask someone at home how their day went, and really listen.
Set one clear intention for today and write it down.
Help with one chore at home without being asked.
Spend ten minutes with the Qur'an before you check your phone.
Speak gently, even when you are tired.
Finish what you started before taking on something new.
Message a relative you haven't spoken to in a while.
Take a short walk and reflect on the beauty of Allah's creation.
Be on time; punctuality honors other people's time.
When you feel stuck, make dua, then take the next small step.
Replace one complaint today with a word of thanks.
Review your goals each week and ask Allah to put barakah in them.
Do your best, then leave the results to Allah.
Drink water, stretch, and step outside; your body is an amanah.
Turn your commute into dhikr: SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar.
Prepare tonight what will make tomorrow morning easier.
Put phones away during meals and talk with your family.
End your day by noting one thing you did well and one to improve.

friday.text: There is an hour on Friday: if a Muslim prays and asks Allah for something in it, He grants it.
The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday.
Friday is among your best days, so send abundant blessings upon me on it.
Whoever bathes, wears perfume, prays and listens quietly to the khutbah is forgiven since the last Friday.
The five prayers, and Friday to Friday, are expiation for what is between them, while major sins are avoided.
Whoever sends blessings on me once, Allah blesses him ten times.
Allah says: I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me.
Allah wrote in His Book: My mercy prevails over My anger.
Allah divided mercy into 100 parts; He kept 99 and sent one to earth, by which creatures show mercy.
Allah is more pleased with His servant's repentance than one who finds his lost camel in the desert.
The Prophet (pbuh) sought Allah's forgiveness and repented to Him more than seventy times a day.
Two phrases light on the tongue, heavy on the scale: SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, SubhanAllahil Azim.
Say 'SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi' 100 times a day; sins are forgiven even if like the foam of the sea.
In the last third of every night, our Lord asks: Who is calling on Me, that I may answer him?
Your dua is answered as long as you are not impatient, saying 'I prayed but got no answer.'
Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, Allah still records it as a full good deed.
No fatigue, illness, sorrow or hurt befalls a Muslim, even a thorn's prick, but Allah expiates sins by it.
Whoever is patient, Allah grants him patience; no gift is better or vaster than patience.
SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu Akbar: dearer than all the sun rises upon.
Say SubhanAllah 100 times: a thousand good deeds are written and a thousand sins erased.
When people sit remembering Allah, angels surround them, mercy covers them, and tranquility descends.
O Allah, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity, and self-sufficiency.
Pray for your brother in his absence, and an angel says: 'And the same for you.'
Allah stretches out His hand at night to accept the repentance of those who erred by day.
O Allah, grant my soul its piety and purify it, for You are the best to purify it.
Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. When you ask, ask Allah.
Allah says: O son of Adam, as long as you call on Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you.
The best remembrance is La ilaha illallah, and the best supplication is Alhamdulillah.
Let your tongue stay moist with the remembrance of Allah.
Supplication is worship.
Your Lord is generous and too shy to return empty the hands His servant raises to Him.
O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You, and to worship You well.
O Allah, Your mercy is what I hope for, so do not leave me to myself even for an instant.
Ask Allah for well-being (afiyah) in this world and the Hereafter.
When the call to prayer is made on Friday, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade.
When the prayer is over, spread through the land, seek Allah's bounty, and remember Allah often.
Allah and His angels send blessings on the Prophet. O believers, send blessings and peace upon him.
Surely, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.
So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me.
I am near. I respond to the call of the caller when he calls upon Me.
Your Lord says: Call upon Me; I will respond to you.
Do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.
My mercy encompasses all things.
Do not despair of relief from Allah.
Indeed, with hardship comes ease.
If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.
We are closer to him than his jugular vein.
You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.
O you who believe, remember Allah with much remembrance.
My Lord, expand for me my chest and ease for me my task.
Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us mercy from You.
Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful.
